title: Psychometric performance and implementation of the DutchClinician-Administered PTSD Scale for Children and Adolescents-DSM-5.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in children and adolescents is often difficult to diagnose due to symptom overlap with other psychiatric conditions and avoidance behaviors from the child, caregiver, or therapist. To improve diagnostic accuracy, the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for Children and Adolescents-, fifth edition (CAPS-CA-5) was developed. This study evaluated its diagnostic accuracy, psychometric properties, and feasibility in routine child and adolescent mental health care in the Netherlands.
METHOD: The CAPS-CA-5 was implemented in four Dutch mental health institutions. Data from 189 interviews with children and adolescents aged 7-23 years were analyzed, alongside measures of trauma, anxiety, and depression. Psychometric evaluation included confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency, interrater reliability, and convergent/divergent validity.
RESULTS: The CAPS-CA-5 demonstrated strong internal consistency (α = .91) and interrater reliability (κ = .81). Confirmatory factor analysis supported thefifth edition, four-factor model. CAPS-CA-5 scores correlated strongly with trauma symptoms and moderately with anxiety and depression. Compared with CAPS-CA-5, clinical judgment showed low sensitivity (44.4%) but high specificity (84.1%), indicating it often missed true PTSD cases. Online training was found feasible and helped clinicians apply the tool effectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The CAPS-CA-5 is a reliable, valid instrument for PTSD assessment in children and adolescents. The CAPS-CA-5 identified more detailed and a higher number of PTSD consistent cases than unstructured clinical judgment and supports individualized case conceptualization and treatment planning. With proper training, the assessment can be effectively integrated into clinical practice, allowing for earlier and more targeted interventions for traumatized children and adolescents.
